data.title: Prototype
data.tagline: A clickable interface model for walking through page order, branches, and recovery paths
data.learningOutcome: You can walk through the main path and a failure return, and identify which business results remain unverified.
data.description: Before a booking page connects to a service, a clickable prototype can take the team from time selection through details and then to a success or failure branch. It helps check whether the paths are complete, but a simulated booking number or confirmation cannot prove a slot is available or an order was saved.

learning.assumes: You have seen wireframes, or shipped code before realizing the flow was wrong.
learning.outcome: You can walk through the main path and a failure return, and identify which business results remain unverified.

distinctions.label: Wireframe
distinctions.explanation: A wireframe is a static layout that cannot be clicked; a clickable prototype walks through the flow, though its content is still illustrative.

distinctions.label: Working product
distinctions.explanation: A finished product connects real data and logic and completes real business; a prototype only demonstrates paths with fake or empty data.

explanation.title: Wireframe: review page structure
explanation.text: It shows content and placement but cannot check a button's destination, a failure branch, or a return path.

explanation.title: Clickable prototype: walk the page paths
explanation.text: Click through the main path, branches, and recovery with simulated content. It does not contact a live service or verify a saved booking.

data.boundary: Clickable does not mean the business feature works. Confirmation, IDs, and form data in a prototype may be simulated; data persistence, permissions, and slot conflicts need checks against real services.

lessonPractice.title: The booking flow is not aligned yet. What should the team check before connecting real APIs?

options.label: Walk through time selection, details, submission, and failure recovery in a clickable prototype
options.feedback: Correct. Walking the main path and a failure branch checks navigation and recovery; only the real service can confirm an actual booking.

options.label: Check where content sits on each page, but do not click through
options.feedback: Static pages cannot show where submission leads or whether users can return after a failure.

options.label: Connect the real booking API first, then test every path with live orders
options.feedback: A live API is not required to review the page flow; a prototype's simulated success must not be presented as a real booking.

data.agentPrompt: First build a clickable booking prototype and walk through time selection, details, submission, and the return path when a slot is unavailable. A simulated booking number may show the page state, but label it clearly as not saved and not connected to a real API. Connect the service only after the flow is agreed.
